title: 2022 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: Let \(ABCD\) be a rhombus with \(\angle ADC = 46^\circ.\) Let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{CD},\) and let \(F\) be the point on \(\overline{BE}\) such that \(\overline{AF}\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{BE}.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BFC?\)

solutions.text:
Extend \(\overline{BE}\) to meet line \(AD\) at \(G.\) Because \(AD\parallel BC,\) we have \(\angle GDE=\angle ECB,\) and \(\angle GED=\angle BEC\) are vertical angles. Also \(DE=EC,\) so \(\triangle GDE\cong\triangle BCE.\) Hence \(DG=BC=AD.\)

Thus \(D\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AG}.\) The circle centered at \(D\) through \(A\) also passes through \(C\) and \(G.\) Since \(AF\perp FG,\) Thales’ theorem places \(F\) on this circle as well.

Because \(DG\) is opposite \(DA,\) \[\begin{aligned}\angle GDC&=180^\circ-\angle ADC\\&=134^\circ.\end{aligned}\] The inscribed angle \(\angle GFC\) subtending arc \(GC\) is therefore \(67^\circ.\) Finally, \(B,F,G\) are collinear, so \[\angle BFC=180^\circ-67^\circ=113^\circ.\]

Thus, the answer is D .
hints: Show that \(D\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{AG},\) making \(AG\) a diameter
